questions.q: As shown in the figure, a long straight conductor with semicircular arc of radius $\dfrac{π}{10}m$~is carrying current $I = 3A$. The magnitude of the magnetic field. at the center $O$ of the arc is: (The permeability of the vacuum $= 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}{NA}^{- 2}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field& \left({B}_{C}\right)$~produced at the centre of a circular current carrying conductor is given by

${B}_{C} = \dfrac{{μ}_{o}I}{4\pir}\theta . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where,~${μ}_{0}$~is the permeability of free space,~$I$~is the current through the conductor,~$r$~is the radius of the circular conductor and~$\theta$~is the angle subtended by the arc at the centre.

From the given figure, it is clear that the arc of the conductor makes an angle~$\pi$~at its centre.

Substitute the known values of the parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required magnetic field.

$\begin{cases}{B}_{C} & = & \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}NA^{- 2} \times 3A}{4 \times \pi \times \dfrac{π}{10}m} \times \pi \\ & = & 3 \times {10}^{- 6}T \times \dfrac{{10}^{6}\mu T}{1T} \\ & = & 3\mu T\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Two particles $X$ and $Y$ having equal charges are being accelerated through the same potential difference. Thereafter, they enter normally in a region of uniform magnetic field and describes circular paths of radii ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ respectively. The mass ratio of $X$ and $Y$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy gained due to potential difference by charged particle:

$KE = qV$

Relation between momentum & kinetic energy:

$p = \sqrt{2m\left(KE\right)}$

Now, radius of the circular path under magnetic field will be given by,

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{p}{qB} = \dfrac{2m ( KE )}{qB} = \dfrac{2mqV}{qB}$

Therefore,

$R ∝ \sqrt{m} ⇒ m ∝ R^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m1}{{m}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{R1}{R2}\right)2$

questions.q: A charged particle carrying charge& $1\muC$ is moving with velocity $( 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} ) ms^{- 1}$. If an external magnetic field of~$( 5\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k} ) \times {10}^{- 3}T$ exists in the region where the particle is moving then the force on the particle is~$\overset{→}{F} \times {10}^{- 9}N$ . the vector~$\overset{→}{F}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the equation of force as,

$\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{V} \times \overset{→}{B}$

$\overset{→}{F} = {10}^{- 6} \times {10}^{- 3}\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 3 & - 6\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(- 30\overset{^}{i} + 32\overset{^}{j} - 9\overset{^}{k}\right) \times {10}^{- 9}N$

questions.q:
The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of an equilateral triangular loop of side $1m$ which is carrying a current of $10A$ is:

[Take ${\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}NA^{- 2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The perpendicular distance of centroid from any side, $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}m$
Magnetic field due to one side.
${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{µ}_{o}I}{4\pir} [ cos{\theta}_{1} + cos{\theta}_{2} ]$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0} ( 10 )}{4\pir \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\right)} \left[$cos{30}^{°} + cos{30}^{°}\right]$
$= \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{\pi}{\mu}_{0}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right] = \dfrac{15{\mu}_{0}}{\pi}$
Net magnetic field $B = 3{B}_{1} = \dfrac{45}{\pi}{\mu}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{\pi} \ttimes$4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}$
$= 180 \times {10}^{- 7}T$
$= 18\muT$

questions.q:
An electron with energy $0 . 1keV$ moves at right angle to the earth's magnetic field of $1 \times {10}^{- 4}{Wbm}^{- 2}$. The frequency of revolution of the electron will be
(Take mass of electron $= 9 . 0 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The frequency of revolution of the electron& is& $f = \dfrac{eB}{2\pim}$, here,~$e$~is charge of electron,~$B$~is magnetic field and~$m$~is mass of electron.

So,~$f = \dfrac{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {10}^{- 4}}{2\pi \times 9 \times {10}^{- 31}} = 2 . 8 \times {10}^{6}Hz$

questions.q:
Consider a moving coil galvanomenter (MCG):
A. The torsional constant in moving coil galvanometer has dimentions  \left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$
B. Increasing the current sensitivity may not necessarily increase the voltage sensitivity.
C. If we increase number of turns $(\mathrm{N})$ to its double $(2 \mathrm{~N})$, then the voltage sensitivity doubles.
D. MCG can be converted into an ammeter by introducing a shunt resistance of large value in parallel with galvanometer.
E. Current sensitivity of MCG depends inversely on number of turns of coil. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) $\tau=\mathrm{C} \theta \Rightarrow\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=[\mathrm{C}][1]$
(B) $\mathbf{C} . \mathrm{S}=\frac{\theta}{\mathrm{I}}=\frac{\mathrm{BNA}}{\mathrm{C}}$;
V.S. $=\frac{\mathrm{BNA}}{\mathrm{RC}}[\mathrm{R}$ also depends on ' N ']
(C) V.S. $\propto \frac{\mathrm{NAB}}{\mathrm{CR}} \quad \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{NR}$
(D) False [Theory]
(E) E [False]
$\mathrm{C} . \mathrm{S} \propto \mathrm{~N}\Rightarrow \because \mathrm{C} . \mathrm{S} .=\frac{\mathrm{NAB}}{\mathrm{C}}$

questions.q: Four identical long solenoids $A, B, C$~and $D$~are connected to each other as shown in the figure. If the magnetic field at the center of $A$ is $3T$ the field at the center of $C$ would be : (Assume that the magnetic field is confined with in the volume of respective solenoid).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $ϕ ∝ i⇒ B ∝ i$, so, the field at the center of $C = \dfrac{3}{3} = 1T$.

questions.q:
A current carrying rectangular loop $PQRS$~is made of uniform wire. The length $PR = QS = 5cm\text{and}PQ = RS = 100cm$. If ammeter current reading changes from $I$ to $2I$, the ratio of magnetic forces per unit length on the wire $PQ$ due to wire $RS$ in the two cases respectively \left({f}_{PQ}^{I}: {f}_{PQ}^{2I}\right)$& is:

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force acting per unit length between two parallel wires is given by,& $f = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pid}$.

Clearly,~$f ∝ {I}_{1}{I}_{2}$

Therefore,~${f}_{PQ}^{I}: {f}_{PQ}^{2I} = \dfrac{I \times I}{\left(2I\right) \times \left(2I\right)} = 1: 4$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : In an uniform magnetic field, speed and energy remains the same for a moving charged particle.

Reason (R): Moving charged particle experiences magnetic force perpendicular to its direction of motion.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The force experienced by the charge particle is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity at all instants as& $\overset{→}{F} = q \left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right).$

Hence, the magnetic force cannot bring any change in the speed of the charged particle. Since, the speed& remains constant, the kinetic energy also remains constant.

questions.q:
Two very long, straight, and insulated wires are kept at ${90}^{o}$ angle from each other in $xy - plane$ as shown in figure.

These wires carry currents of equal magnitude $I$ , whose direction are shown in the figure. The net magnetic field at point $P$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to wire along x-axis:
${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2\pid}\overset{^}{z}$
Magnetic field due to wire along z-axis:
${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2\pid} ( - \overset{^}{z} )$
${\overset{→}{B}}_{net} = {\overset{→}{B}}_{1} + {\overset{→}{B}}_{2} = 0$

questions.q: A square loop of side& $2a$~and carrying current~$I$~is kept in~$xz$~plane with its centre at origin. A long wire carrying the same current~$I$~is placed parallel to~$z$-axis and passing through point~  \left(0, b, 0\right), \left(b > > a\right)$. The magnitude of torque on the loop about~$z$-axis will be :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force acting on wire& $AB$~&~$CD$~are zero

$τ = {F}_{1}cos \theta \times 2a = \dfrac{\mu0}{2\pi}\dfrac{i2}{a^{2} + b^{2}} ( 2a ) \times \dfrac{b}{a^{2} + b^{2}} \times 2a$

$τ = \dfrac{2{μ}_{0} . i^{2}a^{2}b}{\pi\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)}$

questions.q: Two ions having same mass have charges in the ratio $1: 2$. They are projected normally in a uniform magnetic field with their speeds in the ratio $2: 3$. The ratio of the radii of their circular trajectories is,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB} ⇒ \dfrac{R1}{R2} = \dfrac{m{v}_{1}{q}_{1}B}{m{v}_{2}{q}_{2}B} = \dfrac{v1}{q1} \times \dfrac{q2}{v2} = \dfrac{q2}{q1} \times \dfrac{v1}{v2}$

$= \dfrac{2}{1} \times \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.q: Two wires $A$ & $B$ are carrying currents ${I}_{1}$ and ${I}_{2}$ as shown in the figure. The separation between them is $d$ . A third wire $C$ carrying a current $I$ is to be kept parallel to them at a distance $x$ from $A$ such that the net force acting on it is zero. The possible values of $x$ are:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As current in $A$ and $B$ are opposite in direction, net force on $C$ can never be zero if it is kept between
$A$ and $B$ .

$∴ \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}I}{2\pix} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{I}_{2}}{2\pi\left(x \pm d\right)}$
${I}_{1}\left(x \pm d\right) = {I}_{2}x$
\left({I}_{2} - {I}_{1}\right)x = \pm {I}_{1}d$
$x = \pm \dfrac{{I}_{1}d}{{I}_{2} - {I}_{1}}

questions.q: Let $B_1$ be the magnitude of magnetic field at center of a circular coil of radius $R$ carrying current $I$. Let $B_2$ be the magnitude of magnetic field at an axial distance ' $x$ ' from the center. For $x: R=3: 4, \frac{B_2}{B_1}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_1=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{2 \mathrm{R}} \qquad \mathrm{B}_2=\mathrm{B}_1 \sin ^3 \theta \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{~B}_2}{\mathrm{~B}_1}=\sin ^3 \theta=\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^3=\frac{64}{125}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A proton and a deutron ( $q=+\mathrm{e}, m=2.0 \mathrm{u})$ having same kinetic energies enter a region of uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$, moving perpendicular to $\vec{B}$. The ratio of the radius $r_d$ of deutron path to the radius $r_p$ of the proton path is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In uniform magnetic field,
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{m} \nu}{\mathrm{qB}}=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}(\mathrm{~K} . \mathrm{E})}}{\mathrm{qB}}$
Since same K.E
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{R} \propto \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{q}} \\& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\text {deutron }}}{\mathrm{R}_{\text {proton }}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{d}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}} \times \frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{d}}} \\& =\sqrt{2} \times 1 \\& \therefore \gamma_{\mathrm{d}}: \gamma_{\mathrm{p}}=\sqrt{2}: 1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A long straight wire with a circular cross-section having radius $R$, is carrying a steady current $I$. The current $I$ is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. Then the variation of magnetic field due to current $I$ with distance $r  \left(r < R\right) from its centre will be& $
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Ampere's law and noting that the steady current is uniformly distributed over the cross-section of the cylindrical wire.

$B = \left[
\dfrac{{#956;}_{0}Ir}{2\piR^{2}}, r \le R
\dfrac{{#956;}_{0}I}{2\pir}, r > R
\right]$

Thus,~magnetic field~$B ∝ r$~from the centre for $r < R$.

questions.q: Proton with kinetic energy of $1$ MeV moves from south to north. It gets an acceleration of ${10}^{12}m / s^{2}$ by an applied magnetic field (west to east). The value of magnetic field: (Rest mass of proton is $1.6 \times {10}^{- 27}kg$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$∴ K . E . = 1.6 \times {10}^{- 13} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 27}v^{2}$
$v = \sqrt{2} \times {10}^{7}m / s$
$∴ Bqv = ma$
$B = \dfrac{1.6 \times {10}^{- 27} \times {10}^{12}}{1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times \sqrt{2} \times {10}^{7}}$
$= 0.71 \times {10}^{- 3}T$
So,

$B = 0 . 71mT$

questions.q: A deuteron and an alpha particle having equal kinetic energy enter perpendicular into a magnetic field. Let ${r}_{d}$~and ${r}_{α}$ be their respective radii of circular path. The value of $\dfrac{rd}{r\alpha}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$r = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{2mk}{qB}$
$\dfrac{rd}{r\alpha} = \sqrt{\dfrac{md}{m\alpha}}\dfrac{q\alpha}{qd} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{4}}\left(\dfrac{2}{1}\right) = \sqrt{2}$
Hence option $( 2 ) .$

questions.q:
A rod with circular cross-section area $2{cm}^{2}$ and length $40$ cm is wound uniformly with $400$ turns of an insulated wire. If a current of $0 . 4A$ flows in the wire windings, the total magnetic flux produced inside windings is $4\pi \times {10}^{- 6}Wb$. The relative permeability of the rod is

(Given : Permeability of vacuum~${μ}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}NA^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic flux is given by& $ϕ = NBA$, here,~$N$~is number of turns,~$B$~is magnetic field and~$A$~is area.

Given here,~$ϕ = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 6}Wb, A = 2{cm}^{2}, N = 400, I = 0 . 4A$.

Putting the values,~

$ϕ = 400 \times \left({μ}_{r}{μ}_{0}nI\right) \times A$

$⇒ 4\pi \times {10}^{- 6} = 400\left[{μ}_{r} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times \dfrac{400}{0 . 4} \times 0 . 4\right] \times 2 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ {μ}_{r} = 125$

questions.q:
A small bar magnet is moved through a coil at constant speed from one end to the other. Which of the following series of observations will be seen on the galvanometer $\text{G}$ attached across the coil?

Three positions shown describe: (a) the magnet's entry (b) magnet is completely inside and (c) magnet's exit.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(a) When the bar magnet entering the coil the magnetic flux link with the coil increases, and according to the Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the emf will induce in the coil, which in tern induces current and galvanometer shows the deflection towards right.

(b) When the bar magnet is inside the coil no change in magnetic flux link with the coil, therefore galvanometer do not show deflection.

(c) When the bar magnet exit from the coil the magnetic flux link with the coil decreases, and according to the Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the emf will induce in the coil, in opposite direction which in tern induces current and galvanometer shows the deflection towards left.

questions.q: A closely wounded circular coil of radius $5$ cm~produces a magnetic field of $37 . 68 \times {10}^{- 4}T$ at its center. The current through the coil is _____~ $A$. [Given, number of turns in the coil is $100$~and $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $N = 100$,~$R = 5cm$~and~$B = 37 . 68 \times {10}^{- 4}T$

Magnetic field at the centre of circular coil is given by~${B}_{centre} = \dfrac{N{μ}_{0}l}{2R}$.

Putting the values,~

$37 . 68 \times {10}^{- 4} = \dfrac{100 \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times I}{2 \times 5 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

Current through coil is~$I = 3A$.

questions.q: The magnetic field existing in a region is given by $\vec{B}=0.2(1+2 x) \hat{k} \mathrm{~T}$. A square loop of edge $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ carrying 0.5 A current is placed in $x-y$ plane with its edges parallel to the $x-y$ axes, as shown in figure. The magnitude of the net magnetic force experienced by the loop is_____ $\mathrm{mN}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force on segment parallel to $\mathrm{x}$-axis will cancel each other. Hence $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}$ will be due to portion parallel to $y$-axis.
$\begin{aligned}
& F=0.5 \times 0.5 \times 6 \times 0.2-0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.2 \times 5 \\
& =0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.2 \\
& =0.25 \times 0.2 \\
& =50 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~N} \\
& =50 \mathrm{mN}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A proton with a kinetic energy of $2 . 0eV$ moves into a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude~$\dfrac{π}{2} \times {10}^{- 3}T$.~The angle between the direction of magnetic field and velocity of proton is ${60}^{o}$.~The pitch of the helical path taken by the proton is ____ $cm$.~(Take, mass of proton~$= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27}kg$~and charge on proton~$= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is

$K . E = 2eV$

$B = \dfrac{π}{2} \times {10}^{- 3}T$

$\theta = {60}^{o}$

The pitch of the proton is given by

$P = \dfrac{2\pim}{qB} \times vcos\theta . . . ( i )$

By using

~$K = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{2} ⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2K}{m}}$

Substituting the values in equation (i)

$= \dfrac{2\pi \times \sqrt{2mKE} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times \pi \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times \sqrt{2 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27} \times 2 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}} \times {10}^{3}}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}$

$= 2 \times 2 \times {10}^{– 1} = 0 . 4m$

questions.q:
A straight magnetic strip has a magnetic moment of $44 \mathrm{Am}^2$. If the strip is bent in a semicircular shape, its magnetic moment will be _______ $\mathrm{Am}^2$.
(given $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Magnetic moment of straight wire $=\mathrm{mx} \ell=44$ Magnetic moment of arc $\begin{aligned}& =\mathrm{m} \times 2 \mathrm{r} \\& =\mathrm{m} \times \frac{2 \ell}{\pi} \\& =\frac{44 \times 2}{\pi}=\frac{88}{\pi}=28\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two parallel long current carrying wire separated by a distance $2 r$ are shown in the figure. The ratio of magnetic field at $A$ to the magnetic field produced at $C$ is $\frac{x}{7}$. The value of $x$ is _____
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}+\frac{\mu_0(2 \mathrm{i})}{2 \pi(3 \mathrm{r})}=\frac{5 \mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{6 \pi \mathrm{r}} \\ & \mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mu_0(2 \mathrm{i})}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}+\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{2 \pi(3 \mathrm{r})}=\frac{7 \mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{6 \pi \mathrm{r}} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\frac{5}{7} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{x}=5\end{aligned}$
